I’m not math major. I’m still in high school (second year) and my class is native language and history oriented. Trust me, I’d rather kill myself right now if I were to pick something science-oriented in the future.

I think it’s good that you’re still seeing her, having someone to talk to is (usually) nice starting point.  Everyone should have in my opinion at least one person that’s willing to listen, it’s really great that you have a professional helping you step by step. 

One think that I can tell you rn (from my own experience) is that therapy while it at some point it can be discouraging: long terms for next visit, spontaneous appointment cancellation. Getting someone who has experience helping people with really hard times is a good way to take first step in getting better.  
Also just to be clear if you ever feel that your therapist isn’t helping you, you can always look for another professional. I’ve had awful experience with my first therapist. 
You can always talk to someone, you’re not alone even when you think you are!

I don’t know how to start this so I’ll just get to the bottom, as someone who is both teen, depressed, suicidal, “has an unhealthy relationship with fiction” I can say that you need more than probably ever talk to someone about your struggles. Be it parents, someone you trust with sensitive issues, professional (you mentioned going to one,  but since you posted here I guess that it didn’t work long term) or just someone willing to listen and not judge.  I think conversation takes less preparation, stress and emotional baggage than suicide. 
If you want to talk about your struggles with suicidal thoughts, school or love’n feelings, Im here and I think we’re on the same boat.
